diagnostic_evidence.quote: which provides a suitable estimate even when the fractional order

issues.failure_explanation: Lemma lem:frac is correct as an inequality, but E=Theta-R is subtracted by a double sum of positive parts (delta)_+ over all earlier levels. The coefficient of ||phi^k||^2 in E_n is (1/2)[b_{n,k} - sum_{j>k}(delta_{j,k})_+], which can be negative when the order varies, because b_{n,k} is small for n-k large while the delta terms are not. The paper never proves E_n >= 0, or E_n >= c*Theta_n, or any other lower bound. R vanishes only for constant order. Theorem thm:stability therefore bounds a possibly negative quantity plus the dissipation sums, and yields no bound on ||u_h^n||, ||B_h^n|| or the gradient sums. The claim that the functional works for non-monotone nu(t) is unsupported.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Prove a coercivity lemma such as E_n >= c*Theta_n (or E_n >= 0) for the order profiles of interest. This is likely to need explicit conditions on nu(t) and tau. Otherwise restrict the stability claim to the cases where it holds, or replace the functional by another argument.
issues.overall_effect: The advertised stability result, one of the paper's main contributions, is not established for genuinely variable orders. The convergence theorem uses Lemma lem:frac1 and the Gronwall lemma instead, so it is unaffected.
issues.title: Corrected memory functional E=Theta-R is never shown nonnegative or coercive, so the variable-order 'stability' estimate controls nothing
issues.why_classification: The missing coercivity is a new nontrivial lemma that may fail for rapidly varying or non-monotone orders. A valid repair likely excludes the advertised non-monotone regime or needs new architecture.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: In the periodic case, we take $\mathcal{V}=H^{1}_{\mathrm{per}}\left(\Omega\right)^{2}$, $\mathcal{C}=H^{1}_{\mathrm{per}}\left(\Omega\right)^{2}$

issues.failure_explanation: In the periodic case V and C are the full H^1_per spaces, so V_h and C_h contain nonzero constants, for which ||v_h|| <= C||grad v_h|| fails. Zero mean is assumed only for the exact solution, not for u_h^n, B_h^n or the error components xi. The mean of u_h evolves by the fractional equation and need not vanish, for example when the discrete initial data have nonzero mean or f has nonzero mean. The Poincare step and the H^{-1} bounds on f, g are then not justified for the periodic discrete solution.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Define the periodic discrete spaces as zero-mean subspaces and verify that the scheme preserves this (zero-mean data, f, g). Alternatively treat the mean separately.
issues.overall_effect: The periodic-case parts of the stability and convergence proofs rely on an unjustified inequality. The Dirichlet case is unaffected.
issues.title: Poincare inequality asserted on all discrete spaces in the periodic case, where constants lie in the space
issues.why_classification: A standard, local modification of the function spaces and hypotheses fixes it without changing the method, rates or scope.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof takes ||r_1^n||, ||r_2^n|| <= C*tau (the tau^2 term in I_2) from the unproved O(tau) statement (frac_replacement), cited to [Liu2022] with no hypotheses. Assumption assu:regularity gives only bounded first time derivatives and no bound on the second time derivative. With u_t merely bounded, the L1 residual is only bounded by about 2*||u_t||*t_n^{1-nu}/Gamma(2-nu), which does not tend to zero. The O(tau) bound requires u_tt (or weighted second-derivative) bounds, which are neither assumed nor used explicitly.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add a bound on the second time derivative of u and B to the regularity assumption. Include a short lemma bounding the variable-order L1 residual by C*tau^{2-nu^*}, which is at most C*tau.
issues.overall_effect: The temporal rate O(tau) in the convergence theorem is not supported by the stated hypotheses.
issues.title: O(tau) truncation error used without the time regularity that guarantees it
issues.why_classification: Adding a standard regularity hypothesis and a routine residual estimate preserves the method, rate and theorem.

issues.failure_explanation: The weak form contains (1/Re)(grad u, grad v) - (p, div v), whereas the projection uses weight 1 on the viscous term. Hence (1/Re)(grad psi_u, grad xi_u) - (psi_p, div xi_u) = (1/Re - 1)(grad psi_u, grad xi_u), which is nonzero unless Re = 1. The error equation (conv_step2) contains neither this term nor any projection-error viscous or pressure term, so it is exact only for Re = 1. The theorem is stated for general Re.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Define the pressure projection with the 1/Re weight, (1/Re)(grad(Pi_h u - u), grad v_h) - (Psi_h p - p, div v_h) = 0. The velocity part is unchanged, and the proof then goes through.
issues.overall_effect: The error equation and the subsequent estimates are valid as written only for Re = 1, although the theorem is stated for general Re and Rm.
issues.title: Stokes projection defined without the 1/Re weight, so the error equation omits residual viscous terms
issues.why_classification: Rescaling the pressure part of the projection is a one-line local change that leaves the proof structure, rates and scope intact.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: In addition to the stabilization terms included in the discrete formulation, the numerical implementation uses a divergence-cleaning step for the magnetic field after each time step.
the correction (\ref{eq:recalculated_B}) does not in general preserve the prescribed boundary values.

issues.failure_explanation: Theorem thm:convergence concerns Problem prob:fully, which has no cleaning. The reported experiments apply a projection B <- B - grad(phi) after every step, and in the Dirichlet case Dirichlet values are re-imposed afterwards. The cleaned B then enters the L1 memory history, so the computed method differs from the analysed one. The tables therefore verify the cleaned variant empirically, not the analysed scheme. The text does not state this, and no argument shows that the cleaning preserves the error estimate.

failure_location.quote: This behavior agrees well with the theoretical prediction obtained in Theorem \ref{thm:convergence}.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State that the experiments use the cleaned scheme and present them as empirical evidence only. Optionally add runs without cleaning to compare with the theorem.
issues.overall_effect: The claimed agreement between the first-order rates in the tables and the theorem is only indirect evidence for the stated result.
issues.title: Numerical tests with divergence cleaning are presented as confirming the theorem for a scheme that has no cleaning
issues.why_classification: Qualifying the claim or adding comparison runs fixes it locally; no theorem or result is lost.
